data.content_ref: inline:The target commits an internal logical contradiction between its central claim and its own counterconditions. The claim asserts that 'the dilemma dissolves' — a categorical, unconditional dissolution. Yet the target's counterconditions concede scenarios where dissolution fails: 'If scientists actually prefer corroborated theories because they believe them to be true or reliable in an inductive sense.' By listing this as a countercondition (a case where the target's account does not hold), the target acknowledges that the dilemma can persist. A dilemma that survives under acknowledged counterconditions has not dissolved; it has been conditionally avoided at best. The target cannot simultaneously claim categorical dissolution and enumerate live conditions under which dissolution fails. This is an internal inconsistency distinct from the two prior objections (which concerned induction-smuggling and missing cost analysis): it concerns the contradiction between the strength of the claim's universal quantification and the target's own enumerated escape cases.
